title: Applewood Grilled Pork Shoulder Steaks
seoTitle: Applewood Grilled Pork Shoulder Steaks | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Thick-cut shoulder steaks with apple glaze for ten on the grill
subtitle: Thick-cut shoulder steaks with apple glaze for ten on the grill
description: Boneless pork shoulder is sliced into thick steaks, marinated overnight, then grilled over medium-high heat until charred outside and juicy inside. A reduced apple cider glaze finishes on the grill for shine and tang.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Applewood Grilled Pork Shoulder Steaks in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch pork. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate the steaks
steps.instruction: Whisk cider, olive oil, garlic, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Coat pork steaks and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight so flavor penetrates the thick cut. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build the glaze
steps.instruction: Simmer 1 cup cider with brown sugar, Dijon, and vinegar until reduced to a syrupy glaze that coats the back of a spoon, about 12 minutes. Keep warm off heat. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the grill
steps.instruction: Heat grill to medium-high, about 400°F on the grates. Oil grates well so sticky marinade does not tear the crust when you flip. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill the steaks
steps.instruction: Grill steaks 5–6 minutes per side until grill marks set and internal temperature reaches 145°F in the thickest part. Brush with glaze during the final 2 minutes on each side. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F with a 3-minute rest. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.instruction: Tent steaks 5 minutes, then slice across the grain into half-inch strips. Fan on platters and serve with remaining glaze at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Ask the butcher to slice shoulder steaks if your knife skills are still developing—uniform thickness matters.
Keep a spray bottle of water near the grill to tame flare-ups from cider sugars.
Pair with grilled apple halves brushed with the same glaze for a seasonal smoke-night side.
tonightSpread: Sliced pork steaks with extra glaze, roasted potatoes, and quick pickled red onions.
Soft rolls for building apple-glazed pork sandwiches with slaw.
leftovers: Chop cold steak into a hash with diced potatoes and fried eggs for breakfast shift.
Slice thin for Cuban-style pressed sandwiches with pickles and mustard.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shoulder steaks give you pork BBQ flavor without a twelve-hour smoke commitment. They cook in under thirty minutes on the grill and portion cleanly for a hungry line.
mealPrepNotes: Slice steaks uniform—about 1 inch thick—so they finish together. Marinate up to 24 hours in labeled cambros. Glaze can simmer ahead and reheat on the side burner.
